videos.script: Lesson 3 encrypted a column perfectly. Then the key turned up in the server's log. {{log}} That is how encryption usually fails. Not in the algorithm. In where the key ends up. In the code, in a config file, in a query. {{where}} This lesson stops handing keys out at all. A key-management service keeps them, and offers their use instead. Send it a CPF, get back ciphertext. Send the ciphertext, get back the CPF, if you are allowed to. {{service}} Ana starts one, OpenBao, and splits its root key between three people. She gives the website the right to encrypt and not decrypt, and support the opposite. {{policies}} Then she encrypts a backup with a key the backup never holds. She rotates a key without rewriting a single row. And she destroys a key on purpose, to erase data she cannot reach. {{shred}} Every one of those steps is written to an audit log that never contains a secret. {{audit}}
